This page lists all security vulnerabilities fixed in released versions
       of Apache Tomcat<sup>®</sup> 11.x.
Note: Vulnerabilities that are not Tomcat vulnerabilities but have either been incorrectly reported against Tomcat or where Tomcat provides a workaround are listed at the end of this page.
Low: DoS in WebSocket chat example CVE-2026-66299

The WebSocket chat example provided an unbounded buffer for undelivered
       messages.

This was fixed with commit
       <hashlink hash="4e8e3f8964e9653bab427bf794e026c69ee80f2b"/>.

Affects: 11.0.0-M20 to 11.0.24
Users who followed the security guidance to remove the examples web application are not affected.
Note: The issue below was fixed in Apache Tomcat 11.0.20 but the release vote for the 11.0.20 release candidate did not pass.
Important: The fix for CVE-2026-29146 allowed the bypass of the EncryptInterceptor CVE-2026-34486

An error in the fix for <cve>CVE-2026-29146</cve> allowed the
       EncryptInterceptor to be bypassed.

This was fixed in revision <revlink rev="1840057">1840057</revlink> and
       reported as bug <bug>69420</bug>.
Important: Remote Code Execution via session persistence CVE-2026-11111, CVE-2026-22222
If:

• an attacker is able to control the contents of a file; and
  • the server is configured to use the PersistenceManager
then remote code execution is possible. See the announcement.

Applications that do not use non-blocking I/O are not exposed to this
       vulnerability.
Moderate: Multiple weaknesses in HTTP DIGEST authentication CVE-2026-1184
Several weaknesses were identified.
JavaMail information disclosure CVE-2026-33333
An entry whose header carries no severity rating.
Critical: Remote Code Execution via log4j CVE-2021-44228

Apache Tomcat does not ship with log4j. This is not a vulnerability in
       Apache Tomcat.
